passages.text: Listen to Me, O islands; pay attention, O distant peoples: The LORD called Me from the womb; from the body of My mother He named Me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is the Servant of the LORD.
The Servant addresses the islands.
The Servant addresses distant peoples.
The Servant commands them to listen to Him.
The LORD called the Servant from the womb.
The LORD named the Servant while he was still in his mother’s body.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֤וּ אִיִּים֙ אֵלַ֔י וְהַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ לְאֻמִּ֖ים מֵרָח֑וֹק יְהוָה֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן קְרָאָ֔נִי מִמְּעֵ֥י אִמִּ֖י הִזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמִֽי׃

passages.text: He made My mouth like a sharp sword; He hid Me in the shadow of His hand. He made Me like a polished arrow; He hid Me in His quiver.
passages.sermon:
The LORD chose Me to be His Servant.
He made My mouth like a sharp sword.
He hid Me in the shadow of His hand.
He made Me like a polished arrow.
He hid Me in His quiver.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם פִּי֙ כְּחֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֔ה בְּצֵ֥ל יָד֖וֹ הֶחְבִּיאָ֑נִי וַיְשִׂימֵ֙נִי֙ לְחֵ֣ץ בָּר֔וּר בְּאַשְׁפָּת֖וֹ הִסְתִּירָֽנִי׃

passages.text: He said to Me, “You are My Servant, Israel, in whom I will display My glory.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Me.
He called Me His Servant.
He named Me Israel.
He said He will show His glory through Me.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֖י עַבְדִּי־ אָ֑תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֕ל אֲשֶׁר־ בְּךָ֖ אֶתְפָּאָֽר׃

passages.text: But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent My strength in futility and vanity; yet My vindication is with the LORD, and My reward is with My God.”
passages.sermon:
The Servant of the LORD speaks.
The Servant says, “I have worked hard.
I see no result from my labor.
I have used all my strength for nothing.
My effort seems empty and useless.
But the LORD decides what is right for me.
My God will give me my reward.”
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ לְרִ֣יק יָגַ֔עְתִּי לְתֹ֥הוּ וְהֶ֖בֶל כֹּחִ֣י כִלֵּ֑יתִי אָכֵן֙ מִשְׁפָּטִ֣י אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה וּפְעֻלָּתִ֖י אֶת־ אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: And now says the LORD, who formed Me from the womb to be His Servant, to bring Jacob back to Him, that Israel might be gathered to Him— for I am honored in the sight of the LORD, and My God is My strength— He says: “It is not enough for You to be My Servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the protected ones of Israel. I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks now.
The LORD formed Me from the womb.
He made Me to be His Servant.
He gave Me the task to bring Jacob back to Him.
He wants Israel to be gathered to Him.
I am honored in the sight of the LORD.
My God is My strength.
The LORD says this:
It is not enough for You to be My Servant only.
It is not enough just to raise up the tribes of Jacob.
It is not enough only to restore the protected ones of Israel.
I will also make You a light for the nations.
You will bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יֹצְרִ֤י מִבֶּ֙טֶן֙ לְעֶ֣בֶד ל֔וֹ לְשׁוֹבֵ֤ב יַֽעֲקֹב֙ אֵלָ֔יו וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹא יֵאָסֵ֑ף וְאֶכָּבֵד֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וֵאלֹהַ֖י הָיָ֥ה עֻזִּֽי׃ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָקֵ֨ל מִֽהְיוֹתְךָ֥ לִי֙ עֶ֔בֶד לְהָקִים֙ אֶת־ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּנְצִירֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהָשִׁ֑יב וּנְתַתִּ֙יךָ֙ לְא֣וֹר גּוֹיִ֔ם לִֽהְי֥וֹת יְשׁוּעָתִ֖י עַד־ קְצֵ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

passages.text: Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to Him who was despised and abhorred by the nation, to the Servant of rulers: “Kings will see You and rise, and princes will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen You.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Redeemer of Israel.
The LORD is the Holy One of Israel.
The LORD speaks to His Servant.
The Servant was despised by people.
The nation abhorred the Servant.
The Servant served rulers.
Kings will see the Servant and stand up.
Princes will bow down before the Servant.
They will do this because of the LORD.
The LORD is faithful.
The LORD is the Holy One of Israel.
The LORD has chosen the Servant.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה אָֽמַר־ יְהוָה֩ גֹּאֵ֨ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ לִבְזֹה־ נֶ֜פֶשׁ לִמְתָ֤עֵֽב גּוֹי֙ לְעֶ֣בֶד מֹשְׁלִ֔ים מְלָכִים֙ יִרְא֣וּ וָקָ֔מוּ שָׂרִ֖ים וְיִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֑וּ לְמַ֤עַן יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֶאֱמָ֔ן קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיִּבְחָרֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “In the time of favor I will answer You, and in the day of salvation I will help You; I will keep You and appoint You to be a covenant for the people, to restore the land, to apportion its desolate inheritances, to say to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They will feed along the pathways, and find pasture on every barren hill.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel.
The LORD speaks to His Servant.
The LORD says, “In a time of favor, I will answer You.
On a day of salvation, I will help You.
I will keep You safe.
I will appoint You as a covenant for the people.
You will restore the land.
You will give back the desolate inheritances.
You will say to the prisoners, ‘Come out.’
You will say to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’
They will feed along the roads.
They will find pasture on every barren hill.”
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה בְּעֵ֤ת רָצוֹן֙ עֲנִיתִ֔יךָ וּבְי֥וֹם יְשׁוּעָ֖ה עֲזַרְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֶצָּרְךָ֗ וְאֶתֶּנְךָ֙ לִבְרִ֣ית עָ֔ם לְהָקִ֣ים אֶ֔רֶץ לְהַנְחִ֖יל נְחָל֥וֹת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃ לֵאמֹ֤ר לַֽאֲסוּרִים֙ צֵ֔אוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּחֹ֖שֶׁךְ הִגָּל֑וּ עַל־ דְּרָכִ֣ים יִרְע֔וּ וּבְכָל־ שְׁפָיִ֖ים מַרְעִיתָֽם׃

passages.text: They will not hunger or thirst, nor will scorching heat or sun beat down on them. For He who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them beside springs of water.
passages.sermon:
God is compassionate.
God leads His people.
God’s people will not be hungry.
God’s people will not be thirsty.
The sun will not beat down on them.
Scorching heat will not harm them.
God will guide them.
God will lead them beside springs of water.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יִרְעָ֙בוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִצְמָ֔אוּ וְלֹא־ יַכֵּ֥ם שָׁרָ֖ב וָשָׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּי־ מְרַחֲמָ֣ם יְנַהֲגֵ֔ם וְעַל־ מַבּ֥וּעֵי מַ֖יִם יְנַהֲלֵֽם׃

passages.text: I will turn all My mountains into roads, and My highways will be raised up.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises to act.
The LORD will change all His mountains.
The LORD will make His mountains into roads.
The LORD will raise up His highways.
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י כָל־ הָרַ֖י לַדָּ֑רֶךְ וּמְסִלֹּתַ֖י יְרֻמֽוּן׃

passages.text: Behold, they will come from far away, from the north and from the west, and from the land of Aswan.”
passages.sermon:
God gathers His people.
Some people will come from far away places.
Some will come from the north.
Some will come from the west.
Some will come from the land of Aswan.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ אֵ֕לֶּה מֵרָח֖וֹק יָבֹ֑אוּ וְהִֽנֵּה־ אֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִצָּפ֣וֹן וּמִיָּ֔ם וְאֵ֖לֶּה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ סִינִֽים׃

passages.text: Shout for joy, O heavens; rejoice, O earth; break forth in song, O mountains! For the LORD has comforted His people, and He will have compassion on His afflicted ones.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has comforted His people.
The LORD will have compassion on His afflicted ones.
Heavens, shout for joy.
Earth, rejoice.
Mountains, break forth in song.
passages.original: רָנּ֤וּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְגִ֣ילִי אָ֔רֶץ יִפְצְחוּ הָרִ֖ים רִנָּ֑ה כִּֽי־ נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ וַעֲנִיָּ֖ו יְרַחֵֽם׃ס

passages.text: But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!”
passages.sermon:
Zion is the city of God's people.
Zion spoke.
Zion said, "The LORD has left me."
Zion said, "The Lord has forgotten me."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר צִיּ֖וֹן עֲזָבַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה וַאדֹנָ֖י שְׁכֵחָֽנִי׃

passages.text: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God asks a question.
Can a woman forget her nursing child?
Can a mother have no compassion for the son she gave birth to?
Even if a mother could forget her child, I will not forget you.
passages.original: הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ מֵרַחֵ֖ם בֶּן־ בִּטְנָ֑הּ גַּם־ אֵ֣לֶּה תִשְׁכַּ֔חְנָה וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֥א אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands; your walls are ever before Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Zion.
God says, “I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands.”
God always sees your walls.
Your walls are always before Me.
passages.original: הֵ֥ן עַל־ כַּפַּ֖יִם חַקֹּתִ֑יךְ חוֹמֹתַ֥יִךְ נֶגְדִּ֖י תָּמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Your builders hasten back; your destroyers and wreckers depart from you.
passages.sermon: Your builders hurry to return.\r\nYour destroyers leave you.\r\nYour wreckers go away from you.
passages.original: מִֽהֲר֖וּ בָּנָ֑יִךְ מְהָֽרְסַ֥יִךְ וּמַחֲרִבַ֖יִךְ מִמֵּ֥ךְ יֵצֵֽאוּ׃

passages.text: Lift up your eyes and look around. They all gather together; they come to you. As surely as I live,” declares the LORD, “you will wear them all as jewelry and put them on like a bride.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people, Israel.
God is faithful and powerful.
God promises restoration and honor.
Lift up your eyes.
Look around you.
All your people gather together.
They come to you.
The LORD declares, “As surely as I live, this is true.”
You will wear all your people as jewelry.
You will put them on like a bride puts on her ornaments.
passages.original: שְׂאִֽי־ סָבִ֤יב עֵינַ֙יִךְ֙ וּרְאִ֔י כֻּלָּ֖ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ בָֽאוּ־ לָ֑ךְ חַי־ אָ֣נִי נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ כָּעֲדִ֣י תִלְבָּ֔שִׁי וּֽתְקַשְּׁרִ֖ים כַּכַּלָּֽה׃

passages.text: For your ruined and desolate places and your ravaged land will now indeed be too small for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
Israel has places that are ruined.
Israel has places that are desolate.
Israel has a land that was ravaged.
Now, these places will become too small for the people who return.
Those who once devoured Israel will be far away.
passages.original: כִּ֤י חָרְבֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ וְשֹׁ֣מְמֹתַ֔יִךְ וְאֶ֖רֶץ הֲרִֽסֻתֵ֑יךְ כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ תֵּצְרִ֣י מִיּוֹשֵׁ֔ב וְרָחֲק֖וּ מְבַלְּעָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Yet the children of your bereavement will say in your hearing, ‘This place is too small for us; make room for us to live here.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people who once lost their children.
He promises restoration.
Your children, whom you lost, will return.
They will speak to you.
They will say, “This place is too small for us.”
They will say, “Make room for us to live here.”
passages.original: ע֚וֹד יֹאמְר֣וּ בְאָזְנַ֔יִךְ בְּנֵ֖י שִׁכֻּלָ֑יִךְ צַר־ לִ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם גְּשָׁה־ לִּ֥י וְאֵשֵֽׁבָה׃

passages.text: Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has begotten these for me? I was bereaved and barren; I was exiled and rejected. So who has reared them? Look, I was left all alone, so where did they come from?’ ”
passages.sermon:
Israel was once bereaved and barren.
Israel was exiled and rejected.
Israel was left all alone.
Israel sees many children returning.
Israel says in her heart, "Who gave birth to these children for me?"
Israel says, "I was bereaved and barren."
Israel says, "I was exiled and rejected."
Israel says, "Who raised these children?"
Israel says, "I was left alone."
Israel says, "Where did these children come from?"
passages.original: וְאָמַ֣רְתְּ בִּלְבָבֵ֗ךְ מִ֤י יָֽלַד־ לִי֙ אֶת־ אֵ֔לֶּה וַאֲנִ֥י שְׁכוּלָ֖ה וְגַלְמוּדָ֑ה גֹּלָ֣ה׀ וְסוּרָ֗ה וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִ֣י גִדֵּ֔ל הֵ֤ן אֲנִי֙ נִשְׁאַ֣רְתִּי לְבַדִּ֔י אֵ֖לֶּה אֵיפֹ֥ה הֵֽם׃פ

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: “Behold, I will lift up My hand to the nations, and raise My banner to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He is powerful and rules over all.
He says, “Look, I will lift up My hand to the nations.
I will raise My banner to the peoples.
The nations will see My signal.
The peoples will notice My call.
They will bring your sons in their arms.
They will carry your daughters on their shoulders.”
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אֶשָּׂ֤א אֶל־ גּוֹיִם֙ יָדִ֔י וְאֶל־ עַמִּ֖ים אָרִ֣ים נִסִּ֑י וְהֵבִ֤יאוּ בָנַ֙יִךְ֙ בְּחֹ֔צֶן וּבְנֹתַ֖יִךְ עַל־ כָּתֵ֥ף תִּנָּשֶֽׂאנָה׃

passages.text: Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow to you facedown and lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; those who hope in Me will never be put to shame.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to His people.
He promises to honor them.
Kings will serve as your foster fathers.
Queens will become your nursing mothers.
These rulers will bow down to you with their faces to the ground.
They will lick the dust at your feet.
You will know that I am the LORD.
Those who hope in Me will never be put to shame.
passages.original: וְהָי֨וּ מְלָכִ֜ים אֹֽמְנַ֗יִךְ וְשָׂרֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ מֵינִ֣יקֹתַ֔יִךְ אַפַּ֗יִם אֶ֚רֶץ יִשְׁתַּ֣חֲווּ לָ֔ךְ וַעֲפַ֥ר רַגְלַ֖יִךְ יְלַחֵ֑כוּ וְיָדַ֙עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יֵבֹ֖שׁוּ קוָֹֽי׃ס

passages.text: Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to His people.
He asks a question.
Can anyone take plunder from a strong warrior?
Can anyone rescue captives from a powerful tyrant?
passages.original: הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר מַלְק֑וֹחַ וְאִם־ שְׁבִ֥י צַדִּ֖יק יִמָּלֵֽט׃

passages.text: Indeed, this is what the LORD says: “Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the plunder of the tyrant will be retrieved; I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with power and authority.
The LORD says this.
Even strong warriors may lose their captives.
Even a tyrant may lose his plunder.
I, the LORD, will fight against those who fight against you.
I, the LORD, will save your children.
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה גַּם־ שְׁבִ֤י גִבּוֹר֙ יֻקָּ֔ח וּמַלְק֥וֹחַ עָרִ֖יץ יִמָּלֵ֑ט וְאֶת־ יְרִיבֵךְ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָרִ֔יב וְאֶת־ בָּנַ֖יִךְ אָנֹכִ֥י אוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood, as with wine. Then all mankind will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your Savior and your Redeemer.
The LORD is the Mighty One of Jacob.
The LORD will act against your oppressors.
The LORD will make your oppressors eat their own flesh.
The LORD will make your oppressors become drunk on their own blood, as if they drank wine.
All people will know this truth.
All people will know that the LORD is your Savior.
All people will know that the LORD is your Redeemer.
All people will know that the LORD is the Mighty One of Jacob.
passages.original: וְהַאֲכַלְתִּ֤י אֶת־ מוֹנַ֙יִךְ֙ אֶת־ בְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְכֶעָסִ֖יס דָּמָ֣ם יִשְׁכָּר֑וּן וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל־ בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ אֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃ס
